questions.q: A VP of Sales Operations is accountable for whether the Account object's data is accurate and fit for purpose, without personally fixing records. Which role is this?
options: Data owner
Data steward
System owner
Business process owner
questions.explain: The data owner is the business-side role accountable for a dataset's accuracy and fit for purpose; they make the call but don't necessarily do the technical work themselves.

questions.q: A Salesforce admin who manages org uptime, licensing, and release schedules, but has no say in whether the Industry field is populated correctly, holds which role?
options: Data steward
Data owner
System owner
Governance committee
questions.explain: The system owner is accountable for the platform itself (the Salesforce org), which is a distinct concern from the accuracy of the data living on it.

questions.q: In a RACI matrix applied to the Account object, why must 'Accountable' be assigned to a single role rather than split across departments?
options: Because Salesforce only allows one profile to edit any object
Because a single accountable role is required for licensing compliance
Because splitting accountability across departments recreates the stalemate the matrix was meant to resolve
Because only System Administrators are legally permitted to be accountable for data
questions.explain: Consulted can include several departments, but Accountable must be one role with final say — otherwise disagreements between departments have no resolution path, which is the exact problem the matrix exists to fix.

questions.q: Marketing wants 40 new fields on Account; Sales objects, citing clutter and rising duplicates. Without an assigned data owner, how does this dispute typically get resolved in practice?
options: By whichever team's sponsor escalates loudest, or by the admin who picks up the ticket
Automatically, by Salesforce's built-in field-governance engine
By the data steward, since stewardship includes final approval authority
It cannot be resolved until a Salesforce Technical Architect certification is obtained
questions.explain: Without an explicitly assigned data owner, ownership decisions default to whoever has the loudest sponsor or the admin with spare capacity — not necessarily the right decision-maker.

questions.q: A business process owner for the lead-to-opportunity process cares deeply about the Lead Source field but does not hold final approval over its structure. What does this illustrate?
options: That business process owners and data owners are always the same person
That caring about a field is sufficient to be its data owner
That a business process owner can be accountable for a process without being the data owner of fields that process touches
That Lead Source should never be owned by a business-side role
questions.explain: Process ownership and data ownership are distinct accountabilities; a role can be deeply invested in a field's behavior within a process without holding the decision rights over that field's structure.
